metadata.case_name: CHAN HO KAN v. MO MAN HO AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: serious injuries to his left eye including diplopia, decreased visual acuity, obstruction of nasolacrimal duct, elevated intraocular pressure and glaucoma; impairment to ocular motility and reduced visual acuity
source: cutting blade of the operating grinder fell on his face, cutting open his left face, causing serious injuries to his left eye, face, lips, jaw and mouth.

P’s left eye deteriorated, for examples, decreased visual acuity, failure of closure, obstruction of nasolacrimal duct, left vertical and divergent squint. He developed diplopia in all direction of gaze and elevated intraocular pressure.

P’s diplopia was equivalent to 100% loss of ocular motility to his left eye. He also suffered from 35% visual acuity impairment to the left eye. These ophthalmic disabilities resulted in 21% impairment of the whole person. From an ophthalmological point of view, the loss of earning capacity is 52.5%.
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration without prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

injuries.description: through-and-through facial laceration and panfacial fractures: fractured maxillary bone and orbit, Le Fort I and II fractures, comminuted and displaced; metallic foreign bodies in nasal cavity; facial scarring and numbness
source: a 10 cm long through and through facial laceration was noted extending from the left infra-orbital region to left upper lip. P was confirmed to have suffered from fractured maxillary bone and orbit, Le Fort I and II fractures. They were comminuted and displaced fractures.
Upper teeth were exposed through the laceration. Open reduction and internal fixation were performed by surgeons for such fractures. Metallic foreign bodies were found in the nasal cavity.
multiple post-traumatic complications including facial scarring, left facial numbness, diplopia were noted.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures involving skull or facial bones

injuries.description: mild conductive hearing loss in the left ear
source: P complained a hearing loss and pulsatile tinnitus in his left ear after the accident.
A test known as Pure Tone Audiogram (“PTA”) was conducted. It confirmed a mild conductive hearing loss in the left ear.
since the symptoms persisted for over 3 years, the disability would remain permanent.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of middle or inner ear

injuries.description: left dural arteriovenous fistula (identified on CT), assessed as pre-existing and not accident-related
source: CT scan was performed. It was shown a left dural arteriovenous fistula supplied by the left middle meningeal artery.
Both experts took the view that this short-circuit from artery to vein, i.e. dural arteriovenous fistula was a pre-existing condition and was not accident related.

injuries.description: mildly displaced fracture of right 12th rib and displaced fractured of right-sided transverse processes of L1-4 with associated swollen psoas muscle; healed but residual right-sided lumbar pain
injuries.body_part: right 12th rib and right-sided transverse processes of L1-4
source: CT scan revealed that P had suffered from mildly displaced fracture of right 12th rib and displaced fractured of right-sided transverse processes of L1-4 associated with markedly swollen psoas muscle.

From review of P’s medical history, they agreed, from an orthopaedic perspective putting aside fracture of the oral-maxillofacial parts, P had suffered from: right 12th rib fracture; and displaced fracture of right-sided transverse process of L1-4.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures of lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: psychiatric conditions including Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder and Moderate Depressive Episode (in partial remission)
source: He was found to have suffered from Moderate Depression Episode and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder after the accident.
Both considered P’s psychiatric problems attributable to the injury; P is now in remission but is still required to undergo psychiatric and clinical psychologist follow-up.
Both experts come to the view that P had suffered from 5% permanent impairment as well as loss of earning capacity attributable to the psychiatric problem brought about by the injury.

manifestations.description: diplopia (double vision) in various directions of gaze
decreased visual acuity of left eye (best visual acuity reduced to 0.2 / 20/100)
reduced ocular motility of left eye (equivalent to 100% loss of ocular motility to his left eye)
10 cm long facial scar on left face (nasolabial to upper lip)
pain and mild discomfort when chewing due to anterior fixed bridge mobility
mild conductive hearing loss and pulsatile tinnitus in left ear

right-sided lumbar and lower costal margin pain; on and off back pain worse with weather change; pain with lifting 2-3 kg; early morning stiffness; requires painkillers; now uses walking stick and cannot stand/walk for long
headache and dizziness (noted as associated with the dural arteriovenous fistula)
post-traumatic stress symptoms, nightmares, flash-backs, poor sleep and depressed mood

treatments_received: hospitalisation at Prince of Wales Hospital for 13 days
multiple surgeries including open reduction and internal fixation for facial fractures
removal of metallic foreign bodies by ENT and ophthalmology teams
follow-up operations for eye, brain, face and oral maxillofacial injuries
regular follow-up at Ophthalmology, ENT, OMS, Orthopaedics & Traumatology, Neurosurgery and Psychiatry departments
treatments_future: may require one future operation for his left eye
regular ophthalmic monitoring of left eye glaucoma every 3 to 4 months
psychiatric and clinical psychologist follow-up (variously recommended every 2 months for 2 years or once every 4-6 weeks for another year)

losses.description: Unable to resume any gainful employment; Court accepted 100% loss of earning
Conspicuous 10 cm long scar on his face causing facial disfigurement and associated symptoms (itchy painful scar)
Mobility impaired due to poor vision and residual back pain; cannot stand or walk for long; requires walking stick

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Can no longer cycle or swim as he used to do on Sundays

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Difficulty preparing food safely (easily cuts himself when chopping, breaks utensils, difficulty judging precise positions and pouring)
Reduced hearing in left ear (mild conductive hearing loss)
Sleep disturbance, nightmares, flashbacks and depressed mood requiring psychiatric treatment

He was found to have suffered from Moderate Depression Episode and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder after the accident. Both considered P’s psychiatric problems attributable to the injury; P is now in remission but is still required to undergo psychiatric and clinical psychologist follow-up. Both experts come to the view that P had suffered from 5% permanent impairment as well as loss of earning capacity attributable to the psychiatric problem brought about by the injury.

comparable_cases.injury_description: facial laceration across right forehead, eyelids, eyeball, nose and lip; right eyeball replaced by an artificial eye; series of operations; dizziness, headache and memory/concentration problems

comparable_cases.case_name: Kan Kwok Cheung v Cheung Chung
comparable_cases.injury_description: left eye injured then removed, artificial eyeball inserted then removed leaving sunken eye socket and scarring; subsequent reduction in vision in right eye due to glaucoma and cataracts; psychiatric symptoms
